- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.1), model often overcorrects downward; add 1–3% to forecast to avoid premature drop.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak for next 5 days.  
- If history shows mean reversion (recent prices trending down from 80+), model often fails to anticipate drop; adjust downward by 1–3% for next 3–7 days.  
- If forecast is consistently 5–10% above true outcome over 3–5 days, apply “mean reversion bias” correction: subtract 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.15), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before next prediction.
